Just about top of descent both the FAs (Flight Attendants) and both pilots heard a high pitched squealing sound and the FAs believed it was coming from Door R1 near the floor. The FAs also reported a vibration in the floor at the bottom of Door R1. The FAs never reported smelling anything. About a minute after the sound started the FO (First Officer) thought he might be smelling something coming from his gasper vent on the forward instrument panel. I couldn't initially smell anything but possibly a few minutes later might have briefly but if we did it was very brief and minor. The FO described it as a hot plastic type of smell but very faint and for just a couple of minutes. The squeal and vibration lasted about 10 minutes and the rest of the flight was uneventful. I filled out an odor form for MX (Maintenance), they said it would help them troubleshoot our issue and therefore I also am filing a report.

Synopsis.Narrative: A320 Captain reported experiencing a "brief" fumes event at the top of descent. Simultaneously, the flight Attendants reported a temporary "high pitch squeal" accompanied by a floor vibration.

1.Text: Loss Blue Hyd system. Applied QRH procedures and advised ATC.

2.Text: Approximately 200 nm south of ZZZ we received our first indication of any issue with the blue hydraulic system. In level cruise flight we received an ECAM for HYD B SYS LO PR. While running the ECAM we noticed that the hydraulic quantity was low. The procedure calls for the Blue Electric Pump to be shut off, and as we did so, we monitored the quantity indicator. As it dropped, we received an ECAM for Hyd B RSVR LO LVL. After running the ECAM, finishing the QRH and conferring with dispatch we advised ATC for the loss of redundant systems. We chose to divert to ZZZ for a multitude of reasons including the nice weather, long runways, availability of ARFF (Airport Rescue and Firefighting) and the fact that it's a maintenance hub. We immediately received vectors and a descent from ATC for an arrival into ZZZ. The Captain finalized his briefings to both the flight attendants and passengers. We then updated the FMC, applied the landing distance procedure and landing calculations and briefed the descent and approach. We completed the RNAV to [Runway XX], landed and had ARFF inspect the aircraft for any potential hazards or safety concerns. Once complete, we taxied to the gate and completed the diversion safely.

Synopsis.Narrative: A320 flight crew reported a loss of hydraulic pressure that resulted in a diversion.

1.Text: I was the Captain on Flight XXXX, ZZZ to ZZZ1. During the climb, passing FL330 to FL 350, ECAM ADR1. Complying with instructions from ECAM, additional ECAMs: AP 1& 2, A/THR, RUD TRV LIM and GPWS. We also lost both FD (Flight Display). [Advised ATC] and asked for vector to divert to ZZZ2. ZZZ2 weather was clear, ZZZ had thunderstorms. Phone patch with Dispatch and [Maintenance Control] and advised of situations and intentions. Descended into ZZZ2. Asked for delaying vectors to get under landing weight. Raw data landing was normal. Completed [Maintenance Manual].

2.Text: I was the First Officer on Flight XXXX, ZZZ to ZZZ1. During the climb, passing FL330 to FL 350, ECAM ADR1. Complying with instructions from ECAM, additional ECAMs: AP 1&2, A/THR, RUD TRV LIM and GPWS. We also lost both FD (Flight Display). [Advised ATC] and asked for vector to divert to ZZZ2. ZZZ2 weather was clear, ZZZ had thunderstorms. Phone patch with Dispatch and [Maintenance Control] and advised of situations and intentions. Descended into ZZZ2. Asked for delaying vectors to get under landing weight. Raw data landing was normal. Completed [Maintenance Manual].

Synopsis.Narrative: Flight Crew reported diverting caused by loss of ADR1 and associated NAV and FLIGHT Displays.

1.Text: On Date, I was the assigned Captain on Aircraft X. The aircraft had the following MEL: APU shutdown during Engine 1 start action. Reset retry no help, request approval to apply MEL action. Applied MEL action, APU surges / rumbles during MES (main engine start) mode. It can carry both packs normally. When [the] First Officer and I were preflighting the aircraft arrived at the gate, the aircraft had already been completely boarded. There was no ground air operating. During the preflight, the ground power failed and the entire airplane went dark. Ramp personnel attempted to reconnect, but the airplane would not accept the power. The Ramp Supervisor, talking with me through the open aircraft window advised he was going to get a second ground power unit. Minutes later, with the aircraft still dark ramp [agents] attempted to connected power. The aircraft powered for just at 30 seconds and went dark again. The Ramp Supervisor stated the he knew both ground power units are working, yet the aircraft would not accept the power. I contacted the Duty Manager, briefed the situation and stated that I was refusing the aircraft. He agreed, stating he would back my decision. I contacted the Dispatcher for the flight, who conferenced in Maintenance Control. I explained the situation and that I was refusing the aircraft - unable to operate. Maintenance Control stated that with both the APU and ground power not working, The aircraft could not be dispatched, so that technically it was not a refusal. During this call, passengers were becoming agitated and wanting off the dark aircraft. Flight attendants and gate personnel began de-planing the passengers. Several were taking video while in the dark airplane with no air. Maintenance arrived at the airplane during the passenger exit and advised they were able to get the power to work, "the connection was not good." The Dispatcher called, conferenced Maintenance Control, and we again briefed what I have stated so far in this report. Both stated that the refusal was completely understandable and advised with questionable contingencies: what happens if the ground power doesn't work in ZZZ, what if it does work during an unplanned divert, etc. additionally, with passengers filming, said it was the prudent call to refuse the aircraft. The aircraft was powered down so no MRM (maintenance report message) could be sent.

Synopsis.Narrative: Captain refused aircraft after aircraft would not accept external power with an APU already on MEL.

1.Text: This [anomaly] was isolated to the APU bleed and even when MX (Maintenance) was still smelling the odor they still signed the aircraft off, given that it went away with engine start. An APU MEL should have been the first thing they did here instead of trying to get the aircraft back out into service. I as Captain was doing the preflight for our flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1. During the preflight we had a fume event once I selected the APU bleed on. The estimated duration of the event was about one minute. The foul smell came on very strong and immediate. Even with our face coverings (per COVID policy) on in the cockpit it still overwhelmed us, it was that strong. I immediately turned the APU bleed off and opened the cockpit windows. Maintenance then came to the aircraft and did their procedure agreeing the smell was throughout the entire aircraft and coming through on both packs. MX did their procedure and once it was returned to service I had them explain what they did. [MX response] an engine run at the gate and a pack burn. Once we stepped back on the aircraft we still could smell the lingering odor and when I asked about it he said, â€œoh it goes away once you get the engine started". I believe they knew it was still an issue and still signed it off. With the windows open we turned on the APU bleed again and once again the smell came back. This time sending my First Officer and two flight attendants to the hospital. This also resulted in the cancellation of the flight. When I asked about why they didn't just defer the APU in the first place I heard from someone that the high pressure air cart was broken.

Synopsis.Narrative: A320 Captain reported a fumes event during pre-flight and had Maintenance take corrective action. Maintenance worked on it and signed it off as functional, but the crew reported it was still an issue as the smell returned resulting in cancellation of the flight.

1.Text: Enroute ZZZ-ZZZ1 on the red-eye at FL 33,000 ft. into the flight we had an ANTI ICE STBY PITOT ECAM. QRH was used. later we were at FL 35,000 ft. and Autopilot 1 disconnected, I attempted to reengage #1 or #2 autopilots and neither would engage. The FMAs went blank on both the F/O and my PFDs. Autothrust disengaged and went into Thrust LK. Thrust levers were matched with power setting and IDP switches used. We had our route displayed in the ND on both sides and MCDUs were operating normally. ECAM displayed: AUTO FLT AP OFF (RED) AUTO FLT A/THR OFF (AMBER) L/G SHOCK ABSORBER FAULT (AMBER) Indications looked similar to an FMGC Dual Failure except we had both NDs displaying our route, our MCDUs did not go into a subsystem page and no FMGC (Timeout) was observed. The Shock Absorber Fault ECAM had me thinking this may be a different malfunction that I have never witnessed or a coincidence. We contacted Dispatch/Maintenance via phone patch using the "CALL ME" function on ACARS. Maintenance was perplexed of what was causing our malfunction. They had us reset the Auto Flight C/B's B1 (MCDU 1) B2 (FMG 1) and hold. C/B's were reset with no change. We attempted the Long Reset in the QRH Dual FMGC Failure with no success. Mintenance had no other options available. ATC was advised of our equipment malfunction and our inability to remain in ZZZ airspace. We were cleared down to FL 27,000 ft.. Review of our fuel, weather and capabilities with my F/O. Dispatcher we agreed to continue to ZZZ1 with the caution that if we had additional malfunctions, we would consider ZZZ2 as a divert airport. ATC was given our new suffix with the inability to operate in RVSM airspace. Purser was informed of our status. Prior to touchdown at FL 27,000 ft. both FMAs began to populate. Autopilots and Autothrust became available. All malfunctions except for the STBY Pitot cleared. We reengaged the Auto flight functions and remained at FL 27,000 ft. We landed on Runway XX at ZZZ1. Malfunctions were recorded on in the ELB, including a information writeup of what happened. Technician met the plane and we explained what happened.

Synopsis.Narrative: Captain reported failure of aircraft display systems, causing aircraft to descend out of RVSM airspace.

1.Text: I was CA (Captain) and PM (Pilot Monitoring). Departed late due to ELAC (Elevator & Aileron Computer) 1 MEL (Minimum Equipment List). South of ZZZ at FL390, we had ECAM for HYD (Hydraulic) G RSVR (Reservoir) LO AIR PR (Low Air Pressure). I ran the ECAM and told ATC we had a HYD issue. ECAM put us into ATL LAW (Alternate Law) and FO (First Officer) had to hand fly. We asked for lower altitude and told ATC we wanted ZZZ1 and I sent ACARS to Dispatch. I was running the COM and getting ATIS and found out ZZZ was showing 002OVC (200' Overcast) and 1 1/2 vis (Visibility). I asked ATC if there was anything better for weather and he said the region was all the same. We decided to go to ZZZ. Once the COM was complete I called and briefed the FA's (Flight Attendants) and made PA to the passengers. We decided that I would take over and fly the approach and landing. We briefed the ILS 11 Approach and the FO hand flew the Aircraft until about 15-20 mile final so I could take my time and take a few minutes to "gather my thoughts." We started to configure early and we had to gravity extend the gear. Now we were in direct law and started to fly the approach.. We saw the approach lights and continued and saw the runway at minimums. We landed. We taxied to the gate and briefed the passengers and deplaned. I made the phone calls to Company, Dispatch and Maintenance. Maintenance looked at the issue and found out there was HYD fluid all over and we had a bad O ring. They fixed the issue and we were about to land in ZZZ1 about 5 hours late.

Synopsis.Narrative: A320 Captain reported a Hydraulic System Failure inflight resulting in a diversion.

1.Text: I am filing this for the technician that was tasked with this job. Aircraft X had a log to flush blue system hydraulics due to contaminated hydraulic fluid. The procedure in the AMM called out for a tool to purify the hydraulic fluid which [our] company didn't have. The mechanics were then told to follow the AMM until they came to a "roadblock" and then figure it out from there. Eventually they used the Hydraulic Mule, which got contaminated, and figured out a way to flush it through the RAT (Ram Air Turbine) system. Capturing the contaminated fluid became another issue as no one could determine at what pressure this fluid would exit the line. Furthermore, because there was no procedure in place for this task no one could give guidance on what pressure to dial into the Mule in order to get the fluid pushed out (they eventually started at 50 psi and worked their way up to approx 2000 psi which was adequate to complete the task. Whoever wrote the task card should have ensured there was a viable AMM or procedure to accomplish this task and that the correct tooling was in place. We are now aware of several other Airbus aircraft around the system going through the exact same hydraulic contamination issue. In the case of [another] aircraft, it is the Green and Yellow systems that are affected which would necessitate a gear swing if i understand correctly. Could the ERC (event review committee) pleased use all resources to ensure proper procedures and tooling are in place prior to tasks like this one being assigned. Also, is it possible to find out the source of this hydraulic contamination?

Synopsis.Narrative: Technician reported inadequate Task Card and Aircraft Maintenance Manual references, exacerbated by wrong tooling caused difficulties in purging as contaminated aircraft hydraulic system.

1.Text: The mechanic who was assigned to work Aircraft X by chance found that the hydraulic reservoirs and accumulators for the green and yellow systems still had danger tags stating "do not pressurize hydraulics" still hanging from them. These tags were dated XX/Sep/2020 and were from another company.

Synopsis.Narrative: Technician reported finding DANGER, Do Not Operate, tags still installed on hydraulic components on an in service aircraft.

1.Text: The timing of the situation was ripe for a mistake, as a similar-sounding call sign received the exact type of clearance we would have expected as we approached the end of the runway while I was task saturated with completing the required checklist. Ideally, I would not have misheard the call sign, but ultimately I should have realized my attention had been entirely focused on the checklist, not the radio, and asked Tower for a short delay, clarification, or repeated clearance. We were operating the second leg of the day as Aircraft X from ZZZ to ZZZ1. We were given a short taxi from the terminal to Runway XXR. Approaching the departure end of XXR I switched to Tower frequency while still completing the Before Takeoff Checklist. As we made the turn from B onto B5 and while still finishing the last few steps of the checklist, Tower cleared another aircraft with a similar-sounding call sign, to line up and wait on XXC. I mistakenly thought the line up and wait clearance was for us and read back a clearance to line up and wait on Runway] XXR. Tower did not acknowledge my call, and while the Captain and I both saw an aircraft on final for [Runway] XXR, it appeared there was adequate spacing for the line up and wait clearance to be reasonable. As our aircraft passed the hold short line, Tower cleared the similar call sign for takeoff on XXC. The Captain and I simultaneously realized there had been a possible mix up of call signs. We advised tower we had read back the line up and wait clearance and asked for confirmation that it had been for us. Tower advised that it had not been for us, but cleared us for an immediate takeoff to accommodate the aircraft on final for [Runway] XXR. We immediately transitioned to a rolling takeoff and were able to get airborne before any go-around or other action was required by the aircraft on final.

2.Text: It did not sound right to me when the Tower said to line up and wait, but after the First Officer read back the instructions and the Tower did not correct us we pressed on. Next time I am in a situation that does not feel right, I will stop what I am doing and verify the instructions before taking the runway. We were taxiing to Runway XXR in ZZZ. As we were approaching the hold short line we heard the instruction to line up and wait. The First Officer read back "Aircraft X line up and wait XXR." Both of us looked at final approach and saw an aircraft on approximately a 5 mile final, I verified this with my MFD. As we turned on to the runway the Tower cleared an aircraft for takeoff that had a very similar call sign as ours. At this point, I verified our instructions to lineup and wait. Tower said that he did not clear us to line up and wait. The Controller immediately cleared us for takeoff and so we took off.

Synopsis.Narrative: A320 flight crew reported runway incursion.

1.Text: Be fast to recognize an air quality event. I was flying an A320 from ZZZ to ZZZ1. During the arrival we had an air quality event. The estimated duration of the event was 5 minutes. During the event the power levels did not change. I have experienced this in the same type of aircraft before. There was no evidence of smoke or fire in the cockpit and it was localized. The odor smelled like dirty socks and were mild. It was only in the cockpit. During the time of event, our air supply was the engines. I was able to turn off Pack 1 and isolate the problem within about 15 seconds. I reserve the right to change my statement as more informant becomes available.

Synopsis.Narrative: A320 Captain reported a fumes event during descent which was described as a "dirty socks" odor. The flight continued to its destination after the number 1 Pack was turned off.

1.Text: Have more of a warning from ATC of the turbulence expected to encounter. We did not know of the severity of the turbulence until we were in it ourselves. Experienced continuous moderate turbulence between 8,000 feet to 3,000 feet on descent on the RNAV arrival. We landed without incident.

Synopsis.Narrative: Air carrier Captain reported unexpected moderate turbulence during descent.

1.Text: Attempted to de ice as per station procedure for light frost appproximately 10 ft. from the gate. De ice personnel used absolutely no standard phraseology. Sprayed left wing and left for approximately 30 minutes to return for right wing. We were informed by the crew chief that it was for the truck to heat to the required temperature. I asked the crew chief to inspect the left wing. He reported that it was now all ice. The First Officer and I both inspected the wing and it was indeed a significant layer of clear ice. We informed the station manager that the wing and also the right wing would need to be de iced at proper temperature of the fluid. The Crew chief and ramp personnel were extremely diligent. They personally inspected the temperature of the truck ( it was 40 degrees) below the minimum temperature). The crew chief also brought the de ice manual for the truck to the flight deck. We informed the station manger that we could not depart until the truck was verified at the proper temperature ( by the ground crew) and that we would then de ice again and that the FO (First Officer) and I would both visually inspect before leaving the gate area. This entire evolution took 120 minutes. The station managers, gate personnel and especially the ground crew were beyond outstanding. The gist of the episode is that the de icer made the situation much worse by spraying improper temperature fluid and created ice and then informed us that the wing was clear. Had the flight crew and ramp crew not been diligent and inspected it could have been a problem. The de ice crew was improperly trained, completely unaware of procedure and dangerous. The contract de ice company at ZZZ needs to be trained properly in procedure, phraseology and common sense or the contract needs to be awarded to a competent company.

Synopsis.Narrative: A-320 Captain reported the de-icing crew improperly de-iced the aircraft resulting in a dangerous situation and a significant delay.

1.Text: Traveling in level cruise at FL370, smooth air, Mach .80 we experienced an aircraft Mach speed exceedence. With no noticeable wind change the aircraft accelerated, uncommanded, up to Mach .84. The A/T system made minimal, if any, changes to the cruise power setting. The Captain (PF) immediately spun the Mach speed way back and extended full speed brakes. This was the point at which the A/T finally brought the power back. We stabilized the aircraft, configured the automation and continued to the destination with no other abnormalities. We possibly could have reacted more aggressively and sooner, but we fully expected the A/T system to respond correctly to the speed increase and reduce power accordingly. Aside from that, I cannot see anything else that could have prevented the situation. I don't know what we could change to prevent this situation again.

Synopsis.Narrative: Air carrier First Officer reported a Mach speed exceedance during cruise. First Officer stated the increase in speed was uncommanded and there was no noticeable wind change either.

1.Text: I was assigned to work Aircraft X while contract vendor was working on the RH wing fuel tanks and fuel tank panels were open. Myself and Crew Member informed our Manager and Supervisor of many safety concerns we had on the work being performed by the vendor. Example of [these] concerns are: Fuel tank pre-entry check list was never filled out by vendor or Supervisor, no fuel-gas concentration readings were recorded. Per A320 fleet AMM (Aircraft Maintenance Manual) 28-10-00-910-002-A. Aircraft supposed to have a rope barrier around the entire perimeter of Aircraft and warning sign on four areas per fig. sheet 1 per AMM. The fuel vendor only roped just one section of Aircraft while having open fuel tank covers. Supervisor and Manager ignored our safety concerns of the vendor improper maintenance procedures and directed us to work next to the open fuel tank areas ( L/H pack Bay ). I felt that Management was making me work under unsafe work environment. Contract vendor not following safety procedures per AMM. Contract vendors and Management need to follow all safety precautions and not ignore them.

Example of [these] concerns are: Fuel tank pre-entry check list was never filled out by vendor or Supervisor, no fuel-gas concentration readings were recorded. Per A320 fleet AMM (Aircraft Maintenance Manual) 28-10-00-910-002-A. Aircraft supposed to have a rope barrier around the entire perimeter of Aircraft and warning sign on four areas per fig. sheet 1 per AMM. The fuel vendor only roped just one section of Aircraft while having open fuel tank covers. Supervisor and Manager ignored our safety concerns of the vendor improper maintenance procedures and directed us to work next to the open fuel tank areas ( L/H pack Bay ). I feel like the company ignored our safety concerns and put pressure and directed us in working on an unsafe work environment per Aircraft AMM. Contract vendors not following the AMM this created a unsafe work environment. Contract vendors are required to follow each step on AMM including completing all documentation of all maintenance performed on Aircraft.

5.Text: I was assigned to work Aircraft X while contract vendor was working on the RH wing fuel tanks and fuel tank panels were open. My self and crew member informed our Manager and Supervisor of many safety concerns we had on the work being performed by the vendor. Example of [these] concerns are: Fuel tank pre-entry check list was never filled out by vendor or Supervisor, no fuel-gas concentration readings were recorded. Per A320 fleet AMM (Aircraft Maintenance Manual) 28-10-00-910-002-A. Aircraft suppose to have a rope barrier around the entire perimeter of Aircraft and warning sign on four areas per fig. sheet 1 per AMM. The fuel vendor only roped just one section of Aircraft while having open fuel tank covers. Supervisor and Manager ignored our safety concerns of the vendor improper maintenance procedures and directed us to work next to the open fuel tank areas ( L/H pack Bay ). I feel like the company ignored our safety concerns and put pressure and directed us in working on an unsafe work environment per Aircraft AMM. Contract vendor not following the AMM. Contract vendor are required to follow each steps on AMM including completing all documentation of all maintanance perform on all Aircraft.
